intro: Describing a building, a sculpture or a painting, and placing it in its style.

palabras.significado: façade, the front of a building
palabras.consejo: The «fachada» is the «face» of a building: what you see from the street. It is written with ch.
In Romanesque the arch is round; in Gothic, pointed. «Arco» is also a violin bow.
It has an accent because the stress falls on the third-to-last syllable: CÚ-pu-la. Theatres and museums have them.

palabras.significado: Romanesque, the style of the 11th and 12th centuries
palabras.consejo: It changes with the noun: «arte románico», «torre románica». It has an accent on the a.

palabras.significado: Gothic, the style of the 13th to 15th centuries
palabras.consejo: It stresses the third-to-last syllable, hence the accent. Barcelona has a «Barrio Gótico», its old town.

palabras.significado: Baroque, the style of the 17th and 18th centuries
palabras.consejo: The rr is strong. It is also said of anything very ornate: «un estilo barroco».
It ends in l but the stress comes earlier, hence the accent: MÁR-mol. Plural: «mármoles».
It sounds es-TA-twa: u and a make a single syllable. No accent is needed.
A painting is done «al óleo». The stress falls on the first syllable: Ó-le-o.
The z sounds like English th: LYEN-tho. Sometimes «lienzo» means the painting itself.
An «autorretrato» is a portrait of oneself: «auto-» means «of oneself».
It is written with j and the stress falls on the second syllable: pai-SA-he.
Plural: «obras maestras». It is said of a painting, a book, a film or a building.
You restore a painting, a building or a piece of furniture. The stress is on the last syllable: rres-tau-RAR.
Ends in -o, so it is masculine: «el estilo».
Comes from «adornar», to decorate. Its family is «adornar» and «adorno».
Here it agrees with «los adornos», plural: «típicos» ends in -s.
The c and z sound like «th» in Spain: «bronce» is BRON-the.
Ends in -ción, so it is feminine and the stress is on -ón.
Past form of «pintar» (to paint). «Pintó» is for he, she or you formal.
«Artista» is used for both men and women: «el artista» or «la artista».
From «construir»: the i becomes y in the third person, so «construyó».
The g sounds like «g» in «go» before i, so SIG-los.
«Restaurar» is to repair an old thing. Here the verb is in the past.
In Spain the z sounds like «th»: lyen-THOS.
Plural form of «conservar». Note the stress falls on SER.
«Enredar» comes from «red», net. Think of something caught in a net.
The c before o sounds like «k»: AR-kos.
The u is silent after g in «gua» only when followed by e or i; here the u is heard: gwar-DAN.
From «oler»: the o becomes «ue», so «huelen». The h is silent.
The g before o is a hard «g», like «go».
«Muro» ends in -o, so it is masculine: «el muro».
It agrees with «muros», plural: «gruesos».
Smaller than a «montaña». The stress is on LI.
Feminine, with «la sombra». The b here sounds soft, like «v» between vowels.
Before a plural noun, it is «otros». Before a singular, «otro».
«Enmarcar» comes from «marco», frame. Think of a picture in a frame.
In Spain, the j sounds like a strong «h»: LON-kha.
«Mercader» is an old word for merchant. Its family is «mercado».
Agrees with «arcos», plural: «apuntados».
The x sounds like «ks»: eks-I-be. The stress is on I.
Feminine plural. Remember the stress: ko-LUM-nas.
«Estatua» is feminine: «la estatua». The -ua at the end sounds as one syllable.
The v sounds like «b»: le-ban-TAR. The stress is at the end.

texto:
**Buildings.** A building has a **fachada** (façade), columns, **arcos** (arches), towers and sometimes a **cúpula** (dome). Three styles come up again and again in Spain: **románico** (11th–12th centuries: thick walls and round arches), **gótico** (13th–15th: height and pointed arches) and **barroco** (17th–18th: movement and lots of ornament).

**Sculptures.** A **estatua** is **de mármol** (of marble), **de bronce**, **de madera** or **de barro**. The material always takes **de**.

**Paintings.** They are painted **al óleo** (in oils) or in watercolour, on a **lienzo** (canvas). There are **retratos** (portraits), **paisajes** (landscapes) and abstract or contemporary styles.

**Describing.** To place things: **en el centro**, **a la izquierda**, **al fondo**. To give an opinion: an **obra maestra** is an artist's best work. If something is worn out, it gets restored: **se restaura**.

piezas.titulo: The facts of a work: «se» + verb
texto:
To give the facts of a building or a painting, use **se** + verb (**reflexive passive**). The verb agrees with what is built, painted or kept:

- **Se construyó** el castillo / **se construyeron** las murallas.
- **Se pintó** el retrato / **se pintaron** los paisajes.
- **Se conserva** en un museo / **se conservan** en un museo.

There is no need to say who did it. For the date use **en** (**en 1656**) or **hace** (**hace poco**, **hace ocho siglos**).

ejemplos.estudio: El castillo se construyó hace ocho siglos.
ejemplos.alumno: The castle was built eight centuries ago.

ejemplos.estudio: Esta estatua se restauró hace pocos años.
ejemplos.alumno: This statue was restored a few years ago.

ejemplos.estudio: Los lienzos se conservan en el museo de la ciudad.
ejemplos.alumno: The canvases are kept in the city museum.
analisis: se conservan en el museo de la ciudad
en el museo de la ciudad

pregunta.texto: Which style has thick walls and round arches?

opciones.explicacion: Gothic is recognised by its pointed arches and its height.
Yes: Romanesque has thick walls and round arches.
Baroque looks for movement and ornament, not thick walls.

pregunta.texto: Which word goes before the material?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: the material of something is said with «de»: de mármol, de bronce.
«En» shows place, as in «en el museo», not material.
«Con» shows company or instrument; the material takes «de».

frase.texto: Al fondo se ve un palacio gótico

piezas.traduccion: In the background you can see a Gothic palace

pregunta.texto: What do you call a painting of a person's face?

opciones.explicacion: A landscape paints countryside, sea or mountains, not a person.
The canvas is the cloth you paint on, not the kind of painting.
Yes: a portrait is a painting of a person's face.

pregunta.texto: Which verb form completes the sentence?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: «el lienzo» is singular, so the verb is too: «se conserva».
That form is plural and needs «los lienzos».
«Conservas» is the «tú» form; here the subject is the canvas.

opciones.texto: la mejor obra de un artista
opciones.explicacion: Yes: a masterpiece is the best thing an artist has made.
A copy imitates another work; it is not an artist's best.
An unfinished work is a sketch, not a masterpiece.
